blocks.explanation:
Yeh Sawal 9 jaisa hi hai: \(2y\) ki series mein shuru ka 1 nahi, to \(1 + 2y\) poori binomial series banegi.
Saabit kya karna hai? \(4y^{2} + 4y - 1 = 0\).
Plan: Doosri aur teesri term ko \(nx\) aur \(\dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!}x^{2}\) se milayenge; do equations se \(n\) aur \(x\) mil jayenge. Phir jama nikal kar equation mein rakhna.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(2y = \frac{1}{2^{2}} + \frac{1 \cdot 3}{2!} \cdot \frac{1}{2^{4}} + \frac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{3!} \cdot \frac{1}{2^{6}} + \dots\)
Saabit karna hai: \(4y^{2} + 4y - 1 = 0\).
Tareeqa: Dono taraf 1 jama karenge; \(1 + 2y = (1 + x)^{n}\) hoga. Doosri aur teesri term ko \(nx\) aur \(\dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!}x^{2}\) se milayenge; do equations se \(n\) aur \(x\) mil jayenge.

1 jama karein
\[1 + 2y = 1 + \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1 \cdot 3}{2!} \cdot \dfrac{1}{16} + \dots\]
Kyun: Binomial series 1 se shuru hoti hai, is liye 1 jama kiya. \(2^{2} = 4\) aur \(2^{4} = 16\) likh kar numbers aasaan kar liye.

Do equations
\[nx = \dfrac{1}{4} \quad (1)\]
\[\dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2}x^{2} = \dfrac{3}{2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{16} = \dfrac{3}{32} \quad (2)\]
Kyun: Doosri aur teesri terms ko general terms ke barabar rakha.

\(n\) aur \(x\) nikalein
\[\dfrac{n(n - 1)x^{2}}{(nx)^{2}} = \dfrac{3/16}{1/16} = 3\]
\[n = -\dfrac{1}{2},\quad x = \dfrac{1/4}{-1/2} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\]
Kyun: Yeh bilkul Sawal 8 wali equations hain, is liye wohi jawab: \(\tfrac{n - 1}{n} = 3\) se \(n = -\tfrac{1}{2}\), aur \(x = -\tfrac{1}{2}\). Dekhiye, do mukhtalif dikhne wali series ek hi binomial se bani hain.

Chauthi term se tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{(-\frac{1}{2})(-\frac{3}{2})(-\frac{5}{2})}{6}\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{3} = \dfrac{5}{128}\]
\[\dfrac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{3!} \cdot \dfrac{1}{64} = \dfrac{15}{384} = \dfrac{5}{128}\ \checkmark\]
Kyun: Agli term bhi barabar, to pehchaan sahi hai.

Jama
\[1 + 2y = \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{-1/2} = \sqrt{2}\]
\[2y = \sqrt{2} - 1\]
Kyun: \(|x| = \tfrac{1}{2} < 1\), series converge karti hai. \((\tfrac{1}{2})^{-1/2} = 2^{1/2} = \sqrt{2}\). Phir 1 minus kiya.
Dhyan dein: yahan jama \(2y\) ka hai, \(y\) ka nahi. \(y\) chahiye ho to \(\tfrac{\sqrt{2} - 1}{2}\), lekin equation ke liye \(2y\) hi kaafi hai.

Equation saabit karein
\[2y + 1 = \sqrt{2}\]
\[(2y + 1)^{2} = 2\]
\[4y^{2} + 4y + 1 = 2\]
\[4y^{2} + 4y - 1 = 0\]
Kyun: Dono taraf square kiya: \((2y + 1)^{2} = 4y^{2} + 4y + 1\). Phir 2 ko left par laya: \(1 - 2 = -1\). Yahi saabit karna tha.
